args.lesson: What worked: one EXEC that read the deadlines straight from the OCDS raw packages, asserted them against the expected values, then generated, folded and validated the ICS and made a minimal page edit with a reverse-restore check. 16/16 checks passed. The dry_run index hash matched (digest 67cb1f7d...). A second EXEC confirmed the published ICS kept CRLF with no bare LF. What failed: read_product does not accept an encoding argument, so byte-level checks need an EXEC. Untested: calendar-client import, the served .ics Content-Type and the download attribute. Next time: when a page carries per-item expiry, attach the expiry duty to every derived artifact (the ICS event for 105246-2026 must be removed at the Dec 7 expiry). Usefulness is a hypothesis; no demand or revenue is established.
